extensions.description: Open-ended extension map. Known sub-fields have explicit sub-schemas below; unknown fields are allowed (extensions is intentionally open for forward compatibility).

iv_identification.description: Phase 6.iv: metadata emitted when identify / effect is resolved via the IV strategy. The identification only establishes existence of a strategy — the specific formula (Wald / 2SLS / LATE) requires an estimation-layer assumption not captured here.

instrument.description: String form of the chosen instrument atom.

conditioning.description: Sorted list of atom strings forming the conditioning set W (empty = basic IV, non-empty = conditional IV).

required_assumption.description: Text describing the estimation-layer assumption needed to produce a numeric answer (e.g. monotonicity for LATE, linearity for 2SLS).

alternatives_count.description: Total number of valid (Z, W) IV candidates found by structural search. The chosen one is always the subset-minimal and lexicographically first; this count reports how many alternatives exist.

late_caveat.description: Fix 6 (v0.1.5, audit follow-up): present only on numerically-resolved IV results. Mandatory disclosure that the kernel-emitted value is LATE (average effect among compliers — the subpopulation whose treatment shifts with the instrument), NOT the population ATE. Conflating LATE with ATE is a known IV-deployment pitfall; renderer / agent MUST surface this caveat before stating the number.

numeric.description: Fix 6: Wald LATE numeric breakdown. Present only on numerically-resolved IV results. Exposes the 4 component conditionals + derived LATE so downstream consumers can sanity-check.

counterfactual_error.description: Phase 5 §C: error reason when a counterfactual query is outside the supported fragment (e.g. non-boolean domain).

llm_proposed_review.description: Fix 3+4 §3.2 (v0.1.5): aggregated audit surface listing every LLM-proposed element in the program (cause edges tagged annotations.source containing 'llm' + probability statements with provenance='llm_prior'). Attached only when at least one such element exists, so single-population non-LLM-prior runs serialise byte-identically to pre-fix. The Skill v3 contract requires the agent's reply to lead with this list before stating any numeric answer.

edges.description: LLM-proposed causal edges. Each entry has from / to atom strings + the verbatim source string (e.g. 'llm_proposal').

probabilities.description: LLM-proposed probability priors. Each entry has the canonical P(...|...) key, the proposed value, the one-sentence reason (validated non-empty by llm_prior_requires_source), and optional population label.

summary.description: One-sentence human-readable summary the agent must surface in its reply before stating the answer. Counts N edges + M probabilities and reminds the user to audit before trusting the result.

mediation_decomposition.description: Phase 6.mediation: decomposition metadata emitted for effect queries that carry a mediator atom. Reports structural identifiability of NDE/NIE and CDE separately; the chosen strategy picks the strongest identifiable form.

mediator.description: String form of the mediator atom.

mediator_valid.description: True iff the mediator lies on some directed X → ... → M → ... → Y path. False means the mediator declaration is structurally incompatible with the graph.

strategy.description: The strongest identifiable decomposition: nde_nie if Pearl 2001 four conditions hold, else cde if backdoor on (X,M) is available, else none. Absent when mediator_valid=false.

adjustment.description: Sorted list of atom strings forming the adjustment set W used to make M1-M4 hold. Empty list when identifiable with no adjustment, or when not identifiable.

failed_condition.description: First Pearl 2001 condition that blocks identification (null when identifiable).

assumptions.description: Assumptions the structural NDE/NIE identifiability claim rests on (Pearl 2001 cross-world conditions, sequential ignorability, no intermediate confounder, consistency). Empty when not identifiable. IDs reuse the renderer assumption glossary.

adjustment.description: Sorted list of atom strings forming the backdoor adjustment set W for CDE.

failed_condition.description: First CDE backdoor condition that blocks identification (null when identifiable).

assumptions.description: Assumptions the structural CDE identifiability claim rests on (mediator-outcome backdoor adjustment given treatment, consistency). Empty when not identifiable. IDs reuse the renderer assumption glossary.

numeric.description: v0.1.4 Fix 1: numeric mediation evaluation against theta. Boolean-treatment MVP. NDE/NIE branch (when nde_nie is identifiable) reports E[Y(treated)], E[Y(control)], E[Y(treated, M(control))] and the derived TE / NDE-at-control / NIE-at-treated. CDE branch (when cde is identifiable) reports per-mediator-value CDE values. Each branch's failure is recorded as nde_nie_status / cde_status with an insufficient_theta diagnostic.

e_y_cross_treated_outer.description: E[Y(X=treated, M = M(X=control))] — cross-world potential with treated outer arm.

e_y_cross_control_outer.description: E[Y(X=control, M = M(X=treated))] — cross-world potential with control outer arm. Needed for the alternative Pearl decomposition TE = NDE_at_treated + NIE_at_control.

nde_at_treated.description: Pearl decomposition with control reference. TE = NDE_at_treated + NIE_at_control.

nie_at_control.description: Pearl decomposition with control reference. Counterpart of nie_at_treated.

confidence.description: Composite confidence score for the whole result; not a statistical confidence interval.

framing_notes.description: Slice A0 advisory channel: per-predicate gaps in variableDeclaration metadata for predicates referenced by the query. Advisory only — does not influence status.

confidence_sources.description: Slice #34. One entry per slot that participated in the confidence min aggregation, carrying the source annotation, the slot's minimum confidence, and an is_weakest flag marking sources tied with the composite minimum. Absent when no slot contributed or the query is structural.

derivation.description: Machine-verifiable reasoning chain. Only present when the runtime attached one (identify / effect / probability / cause / assoc). Constrained to the exact derivation.schema.json shape so an external agent can round-trip through derivation_from_dict and re-run the verifier.

numeric_estimate.description: Phase 7: data-based estimate. For backdoor / front-door / IV queries this is a single ATE point + CI. For mediation queries it carries a ``decomposition`` sub-block with NDE/NIE/TE triples (point + CI each).

first_stage_f_stat.description: iter 120 / IV methods only: first-stage F-statistic for the instrument's effect on treatment after partialing out conditioning W. Stock & Yogo (2005) flag F < 10 as the canonical weak-instrument threshold for single-instrument 2SLS / Wald. Null when computation was degenerate (e.g. n too small, instrument variance ~0).

sensitivity_analysis.description: Phase 8.2 + iter 124: VanderWeele 2017 E-value sensitivity for the numeric estimate. Present for binary outcomes (RR via baseline rate) and continuous outcomes (RR ≈ exp(0.91·SMD) per Chinn 2000). Categorical / object-typed outcomes silently skip this block. baseline_rate is null on the continuous path because the conversion is fully standardisation-based.

sampling_points.description: Phase 14: T values at which the dose-response curve was evaluated. Sorted ascending; first value is the reference (effect=0 by construction).

reference_point.description: Phase 14: T value used as the reference for curve effect calculations (the smallest sampling point).

dose_response_curve.description: Phase 14: predicted average effect on Y of moving T from reference_point to each sampling_point. Length matches sampling_points; the reference point's row has effect=0.

decomposition.description: Phase 7.4 mediation decomposition: point + CI for NDE, NIE, TE, plus the proportion of total effect mediated through M (NIE / TE).

proportion_mediated.description: NIE / TE — the fraction of the total effect that flows through the mediator. Renderer surfaces this directly as the answer to attribution-flavored questions ('X 占多大份额', '是不是因为 M').

estimation_context.description: Phase 7.1: data contract + option snapshot that gave rise to a numeric_estimate. Helps the verifier reason about reproducibility without access to the raw data.

estimator_failure.description: Phase 14: structured failure when an estimator is reachable but produces an unusable answer (overlap insufficient, convergence failure, etc.). Mutually exclusive with numeric_estimate on the same result.

estimator_dependency_missing.description: Phase 14: surfaces when an optional estimator backend (e.g. EconML for dose-response) isn't installed. Carries the install hint so the caller can resolve.

data_gap_report.description: Phase 10: structured 'what data is still needed to validate this causal claim' summary. Null for query kinds that don't carry data needs (cause / assoc) or when no gaps detected. Generator: themis/output/data_gap_report.py — pure function over derivation + investigation_requests + framing_notes + extensions, no I/O.

bounds_result.description: Phase 12: symbolic bounds on the queried estimand when point identification fails. Null when point is identifiable, when bounds method doesn't apply, or for non-effect queries. Generator: themis/output/bounds.py.

precisionBudget.description: Iter 151+152: post-hoc precision budgeting per VISION 2026-04-26 §'输出 (2)'. Tells the user how much more N is needed to halve the current 95% CI. SE ∝ 1/√N → N_new = N_old · (W_old/W_new)². Helper: themis.output.sample_size.estimate_n_for_target_ci_half_width. Iter 160 added relative_width = half_width / |point| so the renderer's '>30% of point' surface heuristic is mechanical instead of LLM judgment; omitted when point is ~0.

name.description: Must match the name of an enclosing sum's bind.name.

valueExpr.description: A concrete literal value or a reference to a bound value variable introduced by an enclosing sum.

value.description: Concrete literal, varRef bound by enclosing sum, or absent (the value is bound externally by the enclosing query's context — e.g., identify query's target or given atoms).

given.description: Valued atoms conditioned on. May be empty. Refers to any model-distribution conditional, not only literal Theta entries.

name.description: Fresh value-variable name introduced by the enclosing sum. Referenced by varRef in the body.

over.description: Atom whose value domain is iterated. Validator MUST enforce that this atom is ground (contains no var terms).

slot_label.description: Identifies which slot this source contributed to. Shapes: 'parameter:P(Y=y|X=x, ...)' for conditional lookups, 'observation:X=value' for observed atoms.

source.description: Verbatim annotations.source of the statement that pinned this slot (e.g. 'PubMed:12345', 'user_report'). Absent when the contributing statement had no source field set.

is_weakest.description: True when this source's confidence equals the composite min — i.e. this source is (one of) the binding constraints on the overall result confidence.

parameterSkeleton.description: Paste-ready stub for a missing probability CPT entry. Emitted by the investigation_pusher as investigationItem.skeleton when the MissingKind is 'parameter'. Round-trippable into a kernel_ast probabilityStatement once the user fills the numeric value.

value.description: Null in the freshly-emitted skeleton; the user fills it in before merging back via apply_patch_and_run. Once set, must fall in [0, 1] (enforced by merge).

annotations.description: Free-form metadata carried through merge (e.g. {"source": "TODO"} on emission, {"source": "user_report"} after fill).

variablePatch.description: Paste-ready stub for framing a declared variable. Emitted by slice F1 (DEFINE_VARIABLE investigation) as investigationItem.skeleton. The user fills nulls in the 'fields' map; 'existing' is read-only context.

existing.description: Read-only snapshot of framing fields already set on the VariableDeclaration. Merge never writes back into this map.

fields.description: Per-field fill surface. Each legal key maps to the kind that A0/F1 reports as a gap. Value null means the user has not filled it yet; any non-null value is interpreted by merge per field semantics.

target.description: Structured identifier matching the originating MissingItem.name.

skeleton.description: Paste-ready statement stub. Exactly one of two shapes — a parameter skeleton (the user fills in 'value') or a variable_patch (the user fills the fields dict). No third shape is accepted; new skeleton kinds land as explicit additions here.

boundsResult.description: Phase 12: symbolic bounds attached when point identification fails. Expressions are over observable distributions; numeric evaluation lives in the future estimator layer.

lower_expression.description: Symbolic expression for the lower bound, e.g. 'max(0, P(Y=1|X=1) - P(X=0))'.

assumptions.description: Method-specific assumptions (Manski natural: empty; Balke-Pearl: IV1/IV2/IV3).

data_required.description: Observable distributions a client must supply to evaluate the expressions.

width_when_uninformative.description: True when bounds collapse to the trivial range (e.g. [-1, 1] for risk difference) — answer is honest but not useful.

dataGapReport.description: Phase 10: top-level structured report on what data / assumptions / structural changes are still needed to make progress on the query. Gaps are sorted by severity (blocking > important > informational), then by derivation order within the same severity tier.

summary.description: One-line natural-language summary of the most blocking gap, or empty string when gaps is empty.

actionable_next_steps.description: User-facing suggestions in order of impact. Each entry is a complete sentence in Chinese; rendering layer reads these as-is.

answer_tier.description: The strongest answer available for an estimand query (effect / identify / counterfactual), stated explicitly so consumers do not infer it from gap-severity ordering. Orthogonal to gap severity: an unidentifiable effect with informative IV / Manski bounds has a blocking gap yet answer_tier='interval'. point = point estimand identified (possibly pending θ); interval = point ID blocked but informative bounds available; none = neither (needs an assumption / stronger data). Absent for cause / assoc / probability queries.

dataGap.description: A single data / assumption / structural shortfall blocking some downstream output. Each gap maps to one or more upstream signals (derivation step, investigation_request, framing_note, verifier check) carried in provenance.

kind.description: Categorical gap kind. Enum extends as new boards (measurement error, g-methods, L3b nested counterfactuals) come online.

signature.description: Sub-classification within the kind. For missing_distribution: 'marginal' | 'conditional' | 'joint'. Omitted for kinds with no sub-shape.

severity.description: blocking = downstream output cannot be produced at all; important = output produced but quality reduced (e.g. needs untestable assumption, only bounds available); informational = caveat / framing note only.

description.description: Free-form explanation of the gap. Renderer translates to user-facing copy via response_rendering templates.

required_data.description: Optional. What kind of data, on which population, on which variables, would close this gap. Generator fills what it can infer; missing fields stay absent.

sampling_point_count.description: Phase 13: distinct X values to sample for dose-response curve fitting (≥4 recommended).

confounders_required.description: Phase 13: predicates the user must measure and adjust for (typically the backdoor set).

time_window.description: Phase 13: recommended measurement schedule for dose-response data collection.

sutva_concerns.description: Phase 13: SUTVA / interference risks to control for in study design.

blocks.description: Which downstream output this gap prevents.

if_provided.description: What becomes possible if this gap is filled (e.g. 'point estimate with bootstrap CI').

alternative_paths.description: Alternative ways to make progress without this exact data (e.g. 'accept Balke-Pearl bounds' / 'add untestable monotonicity assumption').

provenance.description: One gap may be triggered by multiple upstream signals; array allows multi-source attribution. T10-1 verifier checks every ref resolves to a real artifact in the result envelope.

ref_id.description: Stable identifier within the chosen kind: derivation step_id, investigation_request.target, framing_note.predicate, or verifier rule name.

target.description: For a single-item request this is the MissingItem.name. For a grouped request, a short summary ('N items').

group.description: MissingKind.value for parameter/observation/sample/structure/assumption groups, or 'framing' for DEFINE_VARIABLE (slice F1) — items in the same request share a channel.

items.description: Per-item details within this grouped request. Always populated in v0.2 (length >= 1).
